item.title: 26 mil reproducciones · 1617 reacciones | Casi 60 horas después de quedar sepultada por escombros y lodo tras la devastadora riada en Nepal, una niña de 6 años fue encontrada con vida en Timure, cerca de la frontera con China. Un equipo de la Policía Armada buscaba entre las estructuras destruidas cuando uno de los rescatistas escuchó el llanto de una menor. Nada era visible desde la superficie, pero cuando comenzaron a remover los escombros localizaron a la pequeña en un estrecho espacio bajo piedras, madera y fragmentos de construcciones. La niña fue sacada en brazos y parecía inconsciente, pero tras recibir atención de emergencia se la vio despierta y comiendo en un puesto de seguridad. Su rescate ocurrió en un momento en que encontrar sobrevivientes es cada vez más difícil: la riada del miércoles arrasó viviendas, carreteras y puentes en esta región montañosa de Nepal, donde las operaciones de búsqueda continúan entre los escombros. | Noticias Telemundo

item.title: Minnesota removed common carp; lake clarity rose nearly 600% afterward
item.description: Pickerel Lake, Minnesota, has battled significant water quality and algal bloom problems for decades, primarily due to invasive common carp taking over the shallow waters. After their removal in 2009, the lake underwent a remarkable ecological revival, with water clarity significantly improving and native aquatic plants flourishing once more. This successful restoration highlights the pivotal role of addressing invasive species in revitalizing ecosystems. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Watch: Nepal floods: Families search for loved ones amid hope and despair at Kathmandu hospitals
item.description: The death toll in the Nepal flash floods continues to rise, as search efforts continue for over 2,400 missing people, three days after the disaster struck. Inside Kathmandu’s National Trauma Centre, the atmosphere is heavy with confusion, raw hope, and growing dread. Exhausted families clustered around hospital pillars, desperately searching lists of rescued survivors for names they know. Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.description: El pasado miércoles 26 de agosto, la naturaleza nos volvió a recordar su poder: un desprendimiento de hielo y roca en el Himalaya desencadenó una de las peores catástrofes recientes de la humanidad en la frontera entre Nepal y China. item.title: Viking woman’s clothes preserved by her jewellery for 1,300 years
item.description: Danish archaeologists discovered rare Viking textile remains near Varde. Corrosion from jewelry preserved these ancient wool and linen fragments. This discovery offers a rare glimpse into Viking dress from 1,300 years ago. Researchers will analyze the fibers and teeth for more information. Dating the textiles will reveal if ornaments were new or inherited. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Aviation pioneer Glenn L. Martin donated over 2,500 acres in 1954, helping create a refuge for migratory birds
item.description: A former private hunting preserve now serves as a vital wildlife refuge. This refuge protects tidal marshes and wooded ridges for migratory birds. Established in 1954, it has since expanded significantly in size. The area provides seasonal shelter for waterfowl and nesting grounds for many birds. It also supports mammals, reptiles, and marine species, preserving the bay's natural landscape. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A wooden relic that survived the sack of Jerusalem's First Temple was unearthed by archaeologists, now they are finding shocking answers
item.description: In a remarkable find, archaeologists uncovered ancient wooden beams from the destruction of Jerusalem's First Temple, dating back over 2,600 years to 586 B.C. These preserved sycamore beams, covered in melted plaster, are believed to have supported the roof of an inner courtyard. By analyzing the growth rings, researchers have accurately dated this crucial archaeological evidence, providing an extraordinary link to Jerusalem's rich and ancient history. item.title: Three forgotten kings may change the accepted timeline of ancient Assyria
item.description: Research indicates that ancient Assyrian king lists could have neglected to mention several ephemeral rulers. Evidence points to three monarchs who temporarily ascended the throne amid turbulent political times. Their short reigns might have been intentionally omitted from the official historical timeline, raising questions about the accuracy of Assyria's established chronology. item.title: Scientists spent 100 years discovering animals, reshaping where we see Earth’s biodiversity hotspots
item.description: A groundbreaking study has unveiled that taxonomic advancements have reshaped worldwide biodiversity maps over the last century. While reptile and amphibian diversity has markedly changed, bird and mammal distributions have remained mostly unchanged. Australia and Southeast Asia have been identified as key biodiversity hotspots for these groups. Moreover, factors influencing species richness are also shifting, with precipitation emerging as more crucial. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
